intro.title: Role-Based Route Protection
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a React application with role-based route protection. You will learn how to restrict access to certain pages based on a user's role, such as 'admin' or 'user'. The core concept involves using React Router for navigation and conditional rendering to check user roles before allowing access. You will work with TypeScript to define types for roles and user data, ensuring type safety. By the end, you'll create a simple app where protected routes are only visible to users with the correct permissions.
intro.usecase: Role-based route protection is essential in applications where different users have different access levels, such as enterprise dashboards, banking platforms, or content management systems. For example, an admin dashboard might show analytics and user management pages to administrators while hiding them from regular customers. A healthcare portal would allow doctors to access patient records while restricting nurses to only viewing schedules. This pattern ensures sensitive features like financial transactions or confidential data remain accessible only to authorized roles, preventing unauthorized access and maintaining data security.
